claim: polyamory raises the partnership count -> coupling
evidence: best-region ΔTFR +0.016; concurrency raises partnership count but dilutes the dyadic commitment that predicts childbearing (Toulemon); no CNM fertility premium (Moors 2021; Gupta 2024)

claim: polyamorous alloparenting shares child cost -> parity
evidence: best-region ΔTFR +0.018; the only working sub-mechanism is cost-sharing (alloparenting), which is not non-monogamy - it is the communal channel wearing a different label

claim: CNM concentrates mating on high-status men -> excluded-male externality
evidence: best-region ΔTFR -0.015; male reproductive variance rises, the classic polygyny-instability externality (Henrich 2012) - drags coupling

claim: matrilineal descent raises fertility
evidence: best-region ΔTFR -0.000; lowers female childlessness but co-resident female kin COMPETE (Mattison matrilineal puzzle); Mosuo TFR is not high - autonomy up, quantum flat

claim: matrilocal residence -> grandmaternal childcare
evidence: best-region ΔTFR +0.028; the transferable signal is matrilocal proximity delivering deliverable grandmaternal care (Holden-Sear-Mace) - the kin channel, not the descent rule

claim: stacking co-resident female kin pools childcare
evidence: best-region ΔTFR -0.001; same-sex kin crowding turns cooperative into competitive beyond a small optimum (Mattison 2011) - antagonistic, net negative

claim: kibbutz-style full cost-socialisation of a child
evidence: best-region ΔTFR +0.105; the cleanest natural experiment: kibbutzim socialised the marginal cost and held above-average fertility; privatisation cut lifetime fertility 0.65 (Anson-Meir; Ebenstein 2016) - the channel is cost, not communalism

claim: generic cooperative breeding raises fertility
evidence: best-region ΔTFR +0.016; survival benefit robust (Sear-Mace 2008) but the fertility-quantum boost is contested (Strassmann-Kurapati 2010); works through committed kin, not generic community

claim: state-funded universal in-kind childcare
evidence: best-region ΔTFR +0.097; the scalable state-support variant: universal under-3 care raised German fertility ~2.8% (Bauernschuster 2016; Rindfuss Norway) - modest, causal, in-kind

claim: the communal FORM without cost-socialisation raises fertility
evidence: best-region ΔTFR -0.000; the identification: privatised kibbutz kept the form but lost the fertility (Ebenstein) - communalism per se is not the lever

claim: media is a causal fertility channel (antinatal direction)
evidence: best-region ΔTFR -0.004; the best-identified norm evidence runs ANTINATAL: Globo telenovelas lowered Brazilian fertility (La Ferrara 2012), 16-and-Pregnant cut teen births 5.7% (Kearney-Levine 2015) - N is causal, use for calibration

claim: deliberate pronatal media raises fertility
evidence: best-region ΔTFR +0.029; symmetric pronatal efficacy is unproven and weaker (reactance; the E25 propaganda-backfire result); Israel's pronatalism is a whole-society norm, not a campaign

claim: a pronatal norm multiplies structural levers
evidence: childcare×pronatal-N interaction +0.003; roughly additive in-model - the multiplier is weak, the channels are separable

claim: maternal grandmother proximity raises fertility
evidence: best-region ΔTFR +0.034; a living maternal grandmother raised grandchildren born ~2.1, decaying with distance (Engelhardt 2019; Lahdenpera 2004) - a real input, but an endowment not a policy dial, and shrinking

claim: paying grandparents to provide care recreates the effect
evidence: best-region ΔTFR +0.006; buying out the grandmother does not recreate proximity or the commitment that gives kin care its value - monetising kin is a weak substitute

claim: kin buffers the late-tempo fecundability loss
evidence: best-region ΔTFR +0.014; a tempo x kin derivative interaction - kin lets daughters breed earlier/more, buffering late tau; real but the buffer is disappearing with dispersion

claim: legal recognition of plural parents raises fertility
evidence: best-region ΔTFR +0.002; California SB274 / BC Family Law Act are genuine institutional innovations but scoped to child security, touch <1% of births, no quantum effect

claim: the complementary stack childcare + kin + pronatal-N is super-additive
evidence: three-way interaction +0.005; the same-channel overlap keeps it near-additive

claim: state childcare and grandmother care are substitutes that crowd each other out
evidence: childcare×kin interaction +0.001; little overlap in-model

claim: autonomy-lowering pronatal traditionalism raises fertility net
evidence: best-region ΔTFR +0.021; raising quantum by LOWERING women's autonomy erodes the gender-equity-in-the-home root lever (Doepke-Kindermann; Kleven) - dominated once the autonomy cost is priced
